description: The guidance covers household water-treatment equipment in Alberta. This Alberta information source describes household reverse-osmosis water treatment using a fine membrane and storage container. Its abstract reports a production range of 1–5 gallons per day and states that a booster pump is required above 2000 ppm total dissolved solids or when more than 5 gallons per day is required. These are the historical source’s operating statements; the metadata does not specify the gallon convention, test conditions or equipment model. A specific simulation application is not stated. The package lists PDF and EPUB versions of the same revised September 2012 guidance. The record describes physical water-treatment equipment and preserves the limits of the abstract without generalising its values to every reverse-osmosis system. The Canadian Urban Data Catalogue provides descriptive metadata and exact original Alberta distribution identifiers. It labels the collection Open Government Licence - Alberta. Access is through the linked descriptive record; current provider access and actual file downloads are untested. Costs are not stated. No document, workbook, archive or dataset body was fetched, and numerical contents have not been independently checked. Related editions and components are grouped only where the source identifies their relationship.
